proof_nl: For any real number x, frac(x) denotes the fractional part of x. By the defining identity for the fractional part, frac(x) is exactly the remainder after subtracting the floor of x, namely x - floor(x). Hence for every real x, frac(x) = x - floor(x).
solver_summary: This is the defining identity of the fractional-part function.
vetter_reason: The proof matches the lemma exactly: it states the standard identity frac(x) = x - floor(x) for all real x. No substantive gap, drift, or illegal dependency is present.
